articles.title: ‘The Bird Reich’: Atlanta Falcons roasted over throwback logo with Nazi resemblance
articles.summary: Retro design features red, white and black stripes. Social media users draw Nazi Germany comparisons. Falcons’ X post attracts roughly 26m views. Social media erupted in jokes and memes on Thursday after the Atlanta Falcons unveiled a logo that instantly drew comparisons with the imagery of Nazi…
body: The logo – posted by the Falcons on the NFL team’s social media channels – shows the team’s old falcon symbol from the 1960s and 1970s, emblazoned on a background of red, white and black stripes.
The “throwback” design is being used in the run-up to Atlanta’s game against the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday.
But the design prompted an avalanche of comments from social media users who said it resembled iconography of Adolf Hitler’s Nazi Party.
The Falcons’ post revealing the design on X had attracted some 26m views since being published early Thursday.

articles.title: Lewis Hamilton aims to extend career till early 2030s so he can race in African Grand Prix
articles.summary: 41-year-old set on ‘dream to be able to race in Africa’ Rwanda to host despite criticism of human rights record. Lewis Hamilton has said he hopes to remain racing in Formula One until he can take part in the African Grand Prix which is set to take place in Rwanda in the 2030s.
body: Last week F1 confirmed Rwanda was to host the African Grand Prix having concluded a 10-year agreement for the meeting on a purpose-built circuit, with the first race set for the early 2030s. It is lined up to be held on a circuit in Bugesera, 25 miles south of the capital, Kigali, which has yet to be constructed and marks a return to the African continent for the first time since it last held a race at Kyalami, South Africa in 1993.

Hamilton has been championing a race in Africa for some time. The 41-year-old is understood to be currently contracted with Ferrari until the end of the 2027 season, and speaking before this weekend’s US Grand Prix he said he would like to continue racing for at least another four years in order to make it to the meeting in Rwanda.

“I’m now forced to have to stay a lot longer because we have a race in Africa and that’s been my dream to be able to race in Africa,” he said. “So, I have to keep fighting to try and stay fit if I can. If I can still punch out good results over the next year, we’ll keep it going.”
Hamilton would be at least in his mid-40s if he was to continue until 2030. F1’s current oldest driver is 45-year-old Fernando Alonso.

articles.title: O'Neill bemoans marginal moments but are Celtic just not good enough?
articles.summary: Martin O'Neill spoke of refereeing decisions and near misses after the Europa League defeat against Celta Vigo. But is the reality more concerning?
body: Three Europa League games. Three defeats for Celtic. They are 35th of 36 teams in the competition after another European collapse, this time against Celta Vigo.
Only Ararat-Armenia and their inferior goal difference keeps the Scottish champions from propping up the table.

Off the back of Sunday's 7-1 drubbing of Hearts, there was hope Martin O'Neill's team had turned a corner. Instead, the disparity between their domestic dominance and European shortcomings was laid bare once more.
After Mika Baur swept Celtic in front on 47 minutes, they went into their shells and succumbed to a timid 2-1 defeat as Javi Rodriguez struck twice in three minutes.

articles.title: Europa League: Celtic lose to Celta after leading, Mateta returns in Palace draw
articles.summary: Sunderland drop points in 1-1 draw but stay unbeaten. VAR rules out Juventus winner in draw with Rennes. Celtic suffered more Europa League pain as Spanish side Celta Vigo came from behind to win 2-1 at Parkhead.
body: Germany midfielder Mika Baur fired the home side in front just over a minute into the second half to thrill the Celtic fans but Spain defender Javi Rodríguez scored twice in three minutes – a header then an unstoppable drive – to stun the home side who could not find a way back.
It was another damaging Euro night for the Scottish champions, knocked out of the Champions League qualifiers by LASK on a 5-4 aggregate after being 4-0 up at one stage earlier in the season.

Celtic’s ultras group, the Green Brigade, boycotted the game in protest at the running of the club, albeit there appeared to be only a couple of hundred empty seats, while 3,000 raucous Celta Vigo fans helped the noise.
Jean-Philippe Mateta scored on his first start since the opening day but Crystal Palace could not capitalise on a Besiktas red card to produce a winner in their 2-2 Europa League draw in Istanbul.

articles.title: Bournemouth enjoy night to remember as 10-man Milan fail to weather storm
articles.summary: This was a momentous night in Bournemouth’s history, although the truth is they would have been given a far sterner examination by Coventry or Hull. Whatever this rotten impersonation of a Milan side was, it bore no relation to those that forged such a celebrated history.
body: Bournemouth simply swamped the seven-time European champions and, amid a swirling south coast storm that rarely let up, could depart singing in the rain. Amine Adli’s sumptuous late free-kick, curled left-footed from 22 yards, meant they could finish the evening with the flourish they deserved. Their joy was clear at full time and met disapproval from some of Milan’s staff, who appeared to take umbrage in a short-lived fracas near the tunnel afterwards.

It was certainly an abject return to English soil for Ruben Amorim, who could have been excused in seeing this particular week as the opportunity to prove a point. Amorim may view Bournemouth as kryptonite given they beat his Manchester United side by an identical scoreline at Old Trafford in December 2024. As it happens that is where the Cherries head on Sunday. On this damning evidence the modern version of Milan share more than a few similarities with his former employers.

articles.title: Approach African GP with humility, says Hamilton
articles.summary: Lewis Hamilton addresses concerns on human rights grounds about holding an African Grand Prix in Rwanda by saying people should "approach it with humility".
body: Formula 1 has signed a 10-year deal with the central-east African country starting in the early 2030s.

Briton Hamilton, who has campaigned for a race in Africa for many years, said: "I don't get to choose where we go. Naturally, there are problems all over the world today, so I've seen many of the stories. But I think we really have to approach it with humility.

"There's a lot that we don't know. Growing up in England, they never taught us anything about Africa. It needs to be on the curriculum. A lot of the problems they have there are still results of colonialism and the West intervening."

Rwanda's east-central African neighbour, the Democratic Republic of Congo, has filed a case against the country at the International Court of Justice, accusing it of breaching multiple international treaties covering genocide prevention, racial discrimination, women's rights and torture.

articles.title: Humphries withdraws from European Championship
articles.summary: World number two Luke Humphries pulls out of the European Championship in Germany because of gastroenteritis, with Luke Woodhouse throwing a nine-darter in the opening match of the tournament.
body: Humphries was coming into the tournament on the back of winning the World Grand Prix prior to reaching the final of the Swiss Darts Trophy final, which he lost to Jonny Clayton.
Kim Huybrechts came in as his replacement as the Belgian was the highest-ranked player from the 2026 European Tour rankings who had not qualified.
He took advantage of his late arrival as he produced a dominant 6-1 victory against Ryan Searle during Thursday's first round matches in Dortmund.
Huybrechts hit six 180s and had a 67% checkout success as he set up a second round tie against Stephen Bunting, who produced a 160 checkout in a deciding leg against Danny Noppert as he won 6-5.

articles.title: Every player from Alabama to play for the Golden State Warriors - Jason Caffey
articles.summary: The Golden State Warriors have signed, drafted, and traded for players from nearly every U.S. state and many countries around the world. From Alaska to Wyoming and Austria to Zaire, the Warriors have a strong history of seeking out talent necessary for NBA success.
body: Since their beginnings in the Basketball Association of America (a precursor to the NBA) when they got their start as the team representing Philadelphia before they made their move to the West Coast, the organization has consistently pursued talent from a broad range of sources.

For this installment of our series taking stock of the birthplace of every Golden State player to suit up for the franchise, let's take a look at every player from Alabama who has played for the Warriors.
Our focus in this article is Jason Caffey. An alum of Davidson (Mobile, Alabama) high school, he was picked up with the 20th overall selection of the 1995 NBA Draft by the Chicago Bulls.

The Mobile, Alabama native played the first 3 seasons of his pro career with Chicago before he was dealt to the Dubs in 1998. His stay with the team lasted until he was traded to the Milwaukee Bucks in 2000.

articles.title: Verstappen criticises 'unacceptable' COTA surface amid concerns over injury
articles.summary: Max Verstappen revealed concerns over the state of his spine as he unleashed a scathing criticism of the "out of control" bumpy track surface at Circuit of The Americas.
body: The four-time world champion arrives in Austin for Sunday's United States Grand Prix after claiming his first two victories of the season in back-to-back races.
Speaking to the media on Thursday, Verstappen was unexpectedly passionate over the state of the circuit, which is generally considered as one of the most popular among the drivers on the F1 calendar.
"You see also the track state from what I saw in WEC (World Endurance Championship), it was extremely badly bumpy," Verstappen said.

"I'm not really looking forward to that to be honest, for your spine. I was joking about that in the last race but it's not really a joke to be honest because we mentioned this already for years that it's actually getting a bit out of control.

articles.title: He is the ATP title winner who is unbeaten against Jannik Sinner but is now retiring from professional tennis
articles.summary: Not many players can say they have never lost to Jannik Sinner after facing him. Sinner is currently on the injury sidelines, having ended his season early due to a right knee injury.
body: Despite his recent woes, Sinner has still enjoyed a very successful 2026 season, having won his fifth Grand Slam title at Wimbledon and won every single match he has played at a Masters 1000 tournament.
Only three players have beaten Sinner this year, showing just how hard a feat it is to achieve. Mikhail Kukushkin also has a win against Sinner, and he has now retired from professional tennis.
Kukushkin made his ATP Tour debut in 2007, and nearly 20 years later he is still competing.
The now 38-year-old, who represents Kazakhstan, had announced that he would be playing his final tournament at the Almaty Open, where Kukushkin had received a wildcard for.

articles.title: Norris: 'Incredible' Antonelli two levels above Russell all season
articles.summary: Lando Norris believes Kimi Antonelli has done an "incredible job" and performed "two levels above" Mercedes team-mate George Russell this season, in form which has taken the Italian to the brink of a record-breaking world championship triumph.
body: Antonelli looks all but assured to succeed Norris as F1's reigning world champion this year thanks to the 102-point lead he holds at the top of the standings with six races left.

The 20-year-old could become the sport's youngest-ever champion as early as this Sunday's United States Grand Prix if he wins the race and nearest challengers Russell and Lewis Hamilton do not score sufficient points to stay in mathematical contention.
And Norris, who claimed his own maiden crown with McLaren last year, has spoken glowingly about Antonelli's second season of F1 up against the "very good" Russell.
"I think it's very impressive what he's been able to do," said Norris.

articles.title: Bournemouth seal historic win over Amorim's 10-man Milan
articles.summary: Amine Adli scored a fine free-kick to cap Bournemouth's historic 3-0 win over 10-man AC Milan, which continues their brilliant start to their first-ever European campaign.
body: Ruben Amorim's side are far from the standard of the great Milan teams of the past but this is nonetheless a treasured scalp for Bournemouth who, for the majority of their history, could not have imagined they'd play this fixture. The seven-time European champions, humbled by the Cherries.

It was a wet and wild night on the south coast, with the weather fitting for the chaotic first half, which included Milan captain Mike Maignan being sent off for brutally pushing both hands into Tyler Adams' face at a corner.

That recklessness from the goalkeeper brought Bournemouth their second penalty, which was expertly dispatched by Marcus Tavernier after Justin Kluivert had slotted in the first spot-kick following a Koni De Winter handball.
Another dead-ball moment brought Bournemouth's third. It was a wonderful whip from sub Adli - but Amorim would not have been happy with the Milan wall which broke apart to sum up their sloppiness.
